title: Design Detailing, Drawings and Construction Interface
whyItMatters: Contractors do not build your calculations; they build your drawings and schedules. If a critical assumption in your calculation (such as a bracing bay, bearing length, or restraint) is missing from the drawings, it will not exist on site.
introduction: General arrangement (GA) drawings, member schedules, connection and reinforcement detailing, tolerances, movement joints, erection sequence, temporary stability, RFIs, and making calculation assumptions come true on drawings.
objectives: Read and produce clear General Arrangement (GA) drawings, steel/timber schedules, and RC bar bending/reinforcement details.
Detail realistic construction tolerances, minimum bearing lengths, movement joints, and safe erection sequences.
Manage architecture and MEP coordination interfaces (service penetrations, slab drops, facade brackets, RFIs, and hold points).
Audit drawings against calculations so that every assumed restraint, release, grade, and camber is explicitly communicated.
learningGate: Audit a calculation against its drawing and confirm that every assumption in the calculation is made true by the drawing.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate lifting sling tension amplification due to sling angle ([UI1]).
questions.prompt: A precast concrete beam of mass 6.0 tonnes (static weight W = 60 kN) is lifted by a two-leg crane chain sling with a dynamic lifting amplification factor psi_dyn = 1.30 (total factored vertical lift load = 78 kN). Each of the two sling legs is inclined at 60 degrees to the vertical (so cos 60 deg = 0.50). Calculate the axial tension force T in EACH sling leg.
questions.assumptions: Vertical share per leg = 78 / 2 = 39 kN; divide by cos(60 deg) = 0.50.
questions.explanation: Factored vertical load per leg = (60 * 1.30) / 2 = 39.0 kN. Sling tension T = 39.0 / cos(60 deg) = 39.0 / 0.50 = 78.0 kN (at 60 deg from vertical, each sling leg carries the ENTIRE factored weight of the unit, and induces a horizontal compression force of 39*tan(60)=67.5 kN into the beam!).
questions.citation: IStructE Standard Method of Detailing Structural Concrete & CDM 2015
hints: Identify the governing equilibrium or mechanics equation for "Calculate lifting sling tension amplification due to sling angle ([UI1])." and convert all given dimensions and loads into consistent SI units (N, mm, or kN, m) before calculating.
Calculation setup: Factored vertical load per leg = (60 * 1.30) / 2 = ?. Express your final numeric answer in kN.

It eliminates vertical shear deformation across the web depth by forcing the neutral axis to remain coincident with the geometric centroid of the uncracked transformed section throughout both construction and permanent service stages

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate remaining shear area of a steel beam web pierced by an unreinforced circular MEP duct hole.
questions.prompt: A UB section has web thickness t_w = 10.0 mm and overall depth between fillets d_w = 450 mm (gross web shear area = 4500 mm^2).
